transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this roundtable started. We've got Night Frames scheduled to open Friday, and I need to hear final checks from each of you before I can approve the operating package. Technical director, can you walk me through your assessment of the North Facade front projection setup? Rights and partnerships, I need your sign-off on the sponsor logo placement in the projected artwork. And accessibility coordinator, please give me your read on visitor flow through the west gate. Let's go through these one at a time.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a critical issue before we proceed. My post-draft rigging test found that the North Facade cannot safely support the planned front-projection position. I tested the South Arcade as an alternative and confirmed it works with a rear-projection setup using an 18-meter throw. I filed the test report with technical production this morning, but it hasn't been added to your approval packet yet. We cannot proceed with the North Facade front projection as drafted — the South Arcade rear projection is the safe path forward.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a rights issue before we sign off on the sponsor logo placement. My review of the artist's executed license — completed after the sponsor artwork was drafted — found that the licensed work may not contain sponsor logos or paid promotional marks. We can acknowledge the sponsor in printed programs, but the projected artwork must contain no sponsor branding. I haven't yet updated the partnership deck to reflect this. So the current draft package's inclusion of the sponsor logo in the projected artwork is not permissible under the license terms, and that needs to be corrected before we can proceed.

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a serious accessibility issue with the west gate entry plan. My accessibility walkthrough today confirmed that the west gate has a stair-only approach after dusk — visitors using wheelchairs or mobility devices cannot enter that way. They must enter through the east gate, and the accessible route requires the public entry time to be set at exactly 7:30 PM so that route lighting and attendants are in place. I completed the walkthrough today, but the route map is still with the visitor-services team, so I don't have it in hand to share yet. The draft package's west gate entry plan is not accessible as written.
